symptom: PC1 cannot reach Server1 in VLAN 30. PC1 gets an IP via DHCP but pings to the VLAN 30 gateway time out.
topology_note: Router-on-a-stick with sub-interfaces Gi0/0.10 (VLAN10) and Gi0/0.30 (VLAN30). PC1 is on Sw1 access port VLAN30.
show_outputs: GigabitEthernet0/0.10 is up, line protocol is up | GigabitEthernet0/0.30 is administratively down, line protocol is down
expected_fault: Sub-interface Gi0/0.30 administratively shut down, so VLAN 30 has no default gateway reachability.

symptom: New PCs on VLAN 20 fail to receive an IP address and show APIPA (169.254.x.x).
topology_note: DHCP pool VLAN20-POOL configured on router with ip helper-address pointing to 10.0.20.1.
show_outputs: DHCP pool VLAN20-POOL: 0 addresses leased, 0 addresses in pool (pool exhausted / not configured) | interface Gi0/0.20 ip helper-address 10.0.20.254
expected_fault: DHCP pool exhausted (no free addresses) or ip helper-address pointing to the wrong DHCP server IP.

symptom: PC2 has a valid IP and mask but cannot ping any device outside its own subnet, including the gateway.
topology_note: PC2 static IP 192.168.10.15/24, configured default gateway 192.168.10.254.
show_outputs: Router Gi0/1 ip address 192.168.10.1 255.255.255.0 | PC2 arp table: no entry for 192.168.10.254
expected_fault: PC2's configured default gateway (192.168.10.254) does not match the router's actual interface IP (192.168.10.1) - gateway mismatch.

symptom: Users can ping the web server by IP address but cannot browse to it by hostname.
topology_note: Internal DNS server 10.0.0.53 configured; PCs use DHCP-assigned DNS.
show_outputs: ipconfig /all shows DNS Servers: 10.0.0.53 | nslookup www.internal.local: request timed out
expected_fault: DNS server 10.0.0.53 unreachable or DNS service not responding; no A record configured for www.internal.local.

symptom: Hosts on LAN A (10.1.1.0/24) cannot reach hosts on LAN B (10.1.2.0/24) through R1-R2 link.
topology_note: OSPF area 0 between R1 and R2; static route removed after migration to OSPF.
show_outputs: show ip route on R1: 10.1.2.0/24 is not in routing table | show ip ospf neighbor: no neighbors found
expected_fault: OSPF neighbor adjacency never formed (mismatched area ID or hello/dead timers), so 10.1.2.0/24 is missing from the routing table.

symptom: Finance VLAN users can reach the file server on port 445 but not the web app on port 8080.
topology_note: Extended ACL 110 applied inbound on Gi0/0.40 (Finance VLAN) filtering traffic to the server subnet.
show_outputs: access-list 110 permit tcp 10.40.0.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.0.5.10 eq 445 | access-list 110 deny ip any any (implicit/explicit at end)
expected_fault: ACL 110 has no permit entry for TCP port 8080, so it falls through to the implicit/explicit deny.

symptom: Internal hosts cannot reach the internet even though the default route to the ISP is present.
topology_note: PAT/NAT overload configured on R1 outside interface Gi0/2.
show_outputs: ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/2 overload | interface Gi0/2 missing 'ip nat outside' | interface Gi0/1 has 'ip nat inside'
expected_fault: Outside interface Gi0/2 is missing the 'ip nat outside' command, so NAT translation never triggers.

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi clients can reach the internal file server, violating guest isolation policy.
topology_note: WLC maps Guest SSID to VLAN 99; ACL guest-isolation should block VLAN 99 to internal subnets.
show_outputs: interface Vlan99 (no ACL applied) | expected: ip access-group GUEST-ISOLATION in
expected_fault: Guest isolation ACL is not applied to VLAN 99 interface, allowing guest-to-internal traffic.

symptom: VLAN 30 devices on Sw2 cannot reach VLAN 30 devices on Sw1 across the trunk link.
topology_note: Trunk link Sw1 Gi0/1 <-> Sw2 Gi0/1, allowed VLAN list was manually pruned during a change.
show_outputs: Sw1 Gi0/1 trunking, Vlans allowed on trunk: 1,10,20 | Sw2 Gi0/1 trunking, Vlans allowed on trunk: 1,10,20,30
expected_fault: VLAN 30 is not in Sw1's allowed VLAN list on the trunk (pruned), blocking VLAN 30 traffic across the link.

symptom: Intermittent connectivity loss and slow convergence after adding a redundant switch link.
topology_note: Sw1-Sw2-Sw3 triangle topology, no explicit root bridge configured.
show_outputs: show spanning-tree vlan 10: multiple switches showing 'This bridge is the root' inconsistently over time
expected_fault: No primary/secondary root bridge configured, causing root bridge elections to flap (or a port in blocking/forwarding transition).

symptom: Two users report their PCs keep dropping network connectivity intermittently at the same time.
topology_note: Static IP assignment used on lab printers and a few PCs on VLAN 10.
show_outputs: Printer1 static IP 192.168.10.50 | PC5 static IP 192.168.10.50 | switch log: %IP-4-DUPADDR duplicate address 192.168.10.50
expected_fault: Duplicate IP address 192.168.10.50 assigned to both Printer1 and PC5, causing intermittent ARP conflicts.

symptom: PC6 on VLAN 40 can ping some hosts on the same VLAN but not others.
topology_note: VLAN 40 subnet designed as 10.40.0.0/25 (mask 255.255.255.128).
expected_fault: PC6 has the wrong subnet mask (/24 instead of /25), causing it to miscalculate which hosts are local vs remote.

symptom: Branch office cannot reach HQ subnet 172.16.0.0/16 after a static route change.
topology_note: Static route was re-typed with a wrong next-hop during maintenance window.
expected_fault: Static route next-hop 203.0.113.2 is incorrect; should point to 203.0.113.1, the actual WAN link IP.

symptom: Remote admin cannot SSH into R2 despite correct credentials and reachable IP.
topology_note: ACL 10 applied to vty lines restricting management access.
show_outputs: line vty 0 4 access-class 10 in | access-list 10 permit host 10.0.0.5 (admin PC is 10.0.0.15)
expected_fault: ACL 10 on the vty lines only permits 10.0.0.5, but the admin's actual IP is 10.0.0.15, so SSH is blocked.

symptom: Devices in the new Marketing VLAN 50 get IPs from the wrong subnet (VLAN 10's range).
topology_note: ip helper-address on Gi0/0.50 mistakenly still points to old DHCP relay target used for VLAN10 testing.
show_outputs: interface Gi0/0.50 ip helper-address 10.0.10.5 (VLAN10 DHCP server, should be 10.0.50.5)
expected_fault: ip helper-address on the VLAN 50 sub-interface points to the VLAN 10 DHCP server instead of the VLAN 50 pool/server.

symptom: File transfers to Server2 are extremely slow with occasional errors, though connectivity works.
topology_note: Server2 NIC set to auto, switch port manually set to 100/full.
show_outputs: show interfaces Gi0/5: 100Mb/s, half-duplex, input errors 1450, CRC 980, late collisions detected
expected_fault: Duplex mismatch between switch port (fixed full) and server NIC (auto negotiated half), causing collisions and errors.

symptom: Only one internal host at a time can browse the internet; others get connection failures.
topology_note: NAT configured with static one-to-one translation instead of PAT/overload for the LAN pool.
show_outputs: ip nat inside source static 10.0.0.10 203.0.113.5 | no 'overload' keyword present, no NAT pool for remaining hosts
expected_fault: NAT is configured as a single static translation rather than PAT with overload, so only 10.0.0.10 can reach the internet.

symptom: A newly added PC on Sw3 port Fa0/12 cannot get an IP and shows link up/link down flapping.
topology_note: Fa0/12 was supposed to be assigned to VLAN 20 access mode.
show_outputs: interface FastEthernet0/12 switchport mode access, switchport access vlan 999 (VLAN 999 does not exist)
expected_fault: Port Fa0/12 is assigned to VLAN 999, which was never created, so the port is effectively isolated.

symptom: Traffic from LAN reaches the internet but return traffic for some sessions never arrives (asymmetric routing suspected).
topology_note: Dual WAN links with unequal-cost static routes and no policy routing configured.
expected_fault: Two default routes with different next-hops cause asymmetric routing for stateful services (e.g. NAT'd sessions) without policy routing to keep flows consistent.

symptom: Internal server suddenly cannot send SNMP traps to the monitoring station after an ACL update.
topology_note: Outbound ACL 120 tightened last week to restrict server subnet egress traffic.
show_outputs: access-list 120 permit tcp any any established | access-list 120 deny ip any any (no permit for udp 162)
expected_fault: ACL 120 has no permit rule for UDP port 162 (SNMP traps), so trap packets are silently dropped by the implicit/explicit deny.

symptom: Internal website loads over HTTPS but browser shows certificate name mismatch warnings.
topology_note: Internal DNS has a CNAME pointing to the wrong internal hostname after a server rename.
show_outputs: nslookup portal.internal.local: CNAME oldserver.internal.local -> 10.0.5.20 (cert issued for portal.internal.local, not oldserver)
expected_fault: Stale DNS CNAME record points to the old server hostname, causing a TLS certificate name mismatch (application-layer issue, not connectivity).

symptom: Entire branch office loses connectivity to HQ simultaneously; local LAN still works fine.
topology_note: Single WAN serial link between branch router and HQ, recently re-cabled.
show_outputs: Serial0/0/0 is down, line protocol is down (cable disconnected/carrier loss)
expected_fault: Physical layer failure on the WAN serial interface (cable/carrier loss) is taking down the only path to HQ.

symptom: Inter-VLAN routing works for VLAN10 and VLAN20 but a newly added VLAN60 has no connectivity to other VLANs.
topology_note: Router-on-a-stick config; new sub-interface added for VLAN60 but encapsulation missing.
show_outputs: interface Gi0/0.60 ip address 10.60.0.1 255.255.255.0 (no 'encapsulation dot1Q 60' line present)
expected_fault: Sub-interface Gi0/0.60 is missing the 'encapsulation dot1Q 60' command, so it never processes tagged VLAN 60 frames.

symptom: A handful of PCs get correct IPs but wrong default gateway, causing them to fail reaching other subnets.
topology_note: DHCP pool VLAN10-POOL was edited and default-router value was mistyped.
show_outputs: ip dhcp pool VLAN10-POOL: default-router 192.168.10.100 (actual gateway is 192.168.10.1)
expected_fault: The DHCP pool's default-router value (192.168.10.100) does not match the real gateway IP (192.168.10.1).

symptom: Wireless clients near the edge of the building experience frequent disconnects and low throughput.
topology_note: Two APs on overlapping channels 6 and 6 with high power settings in adjacent rooms.
show_outputs: AP1 channel 6, power 100% | AP2 channel 6, power 100% | co-channel interference reported in RF logs
expected_fault: Co-channel interference from AP1 and AP2 both using channel 6 with full power in overlapping coverage areas.

symptom: Server backup job to the offsite backup target fails to start every night.
topology_note: ACL 130 was recently reordered, moving a broad deny statement above the backup permit rule.
show_outputs: access-list 130 deny ip 10.0.5.0 0.0.0.255 any (line 5) | access-list 130 permit tcp host 10.0.5.10 host 203.0.113.20 eq 22 (line 10, unreachable)
expected_fault: ACL 130's specific permit rule for the backup host is placed after a broader deny statement, so it never gets evaluated (ACL order-of-operations issue).

symptom: After enabling a second ISP link for redundancy, some external websites became unreachable intermittently.
topology_note: OSPF redistribution of static default routes misconfigured, creating a routing loop for certain prefixes.
show_outputs: show ip route: 0.0.0.0/0 [110/1] via 10.0.0.2, then flaps to via 10.0.0.6 repeatedly | traceroute shows TTL exceeded loop between R1 and R2
expected_fault: Route redistribution misconfiguration is creating a routing loop for the default route between R1 and R2.

symptom: External partner cannot reach the published web server via the public IP despite NAT and firewall rules seemingly correct.
topology_note: Static NAT configured for public IP 203.0.113.50 to internal 10.0.5.10; ACL permits port 80 only, partner uses HTTPS (443).
show_outputs: ip nat inside source static tcp 10.0.5.10 80 203.0.113.50 80 | access-list 115 permit tcp any host 10.0.5.10 eq 80
expected_fault: Only port 80 is NAT'd and permitted; port 443 (HTTPS), which the partner actually uses, has no NAT translation or ACL entry.

symptom: A printer moved to a new office cannot be reached at its known static IP anymore.
topology_note: Printer physically moved to a new switch port that was previously configured for a different VLAN.
show_outputs: interface FastEthernet0/8 switchport access vlan 20 (printer expects VLAN 10 addressing 192.168.10.0/24)
expected_fault: The new switch port the printer was plugged into is assigned to VLAN 20 instead of VLAN 10, putting the printer on the wrong subnet.

symptom: After a router HSRP failover test, half the LAN lost internet access even though both routers appear up.
topology_note: HSRP configured between R1 (active) and R2 (standby) for the LAN default gateway virtual IP.
show_outputs: R1 Vlan10 HSRP state: Active, priority 110 | R2 Vlan10 HSRP state: Standby, priority 100 | R2 has no route to 0.0.0.0/0 (default route missing)
expected_fault: R2 (the standby HSRP router) has no default route configured, so when it briefly becomes active during failover testing, it cannot forward internet-bound traffic.
